p: The UN Commission of Inquiry reaches the same conclusion from another direction. It traces the
and says the aim of seizing maximum land while minimizing the Palestinian population stems from Israel’s colonizing policies.

That is how settler colonial states have always worked. Law does not sit outside the project. It is the project’s instrument. Military rule in the West Bank rests on emergency regulations the British Mandate wrote in
to subdue the local population. Declaring “State land” has been, in Adalah’s words,
for taking Palestinian land since the late 1970s. Each layer converts dispossession into a legal procedure: a permit denied, a file closed, a petition dismissed, a statute passed.

Seen this way, the evidence describes one logic working across three levels. Statutes define who holds rights. Police, prosecutors and courts decide whom those rights protect. And the Israeli state has moved to shield itself from outside scrutiny, backed by a US government that now sanctions the institutions that try to apply international law.
A state built to secure one people’s dominance over another people’s land will produce exactly this legal order.
